The core design tension

Course medals are the real progression gate. Money arrives much faster than those gates open. That can work for a gentle study companion, but the shop still asks the player to behave like a tycoon: save, compare upgrades, and collect on a schedule.

My recommendation is to lean into the study companion: generous access, useful chapter rewards, and a restaurant that visibly remembers learning. Raising every price would add waiting while leaving the reward problem unresolved.

What deserves to stay

Exact integer accounting; clear wallet/register separation; purchases applied to future production; permanent medal grants; and no economic power locked behind gold perfection. The kitchen/service model is readable and the scene gives upgrades a physical place.

63 existing economy, purchase and medal checks passed. That supports mechanical correctness. It does not establish player satisfaction or retention.

01 / The findings

Where the balance disappoints

Six findings, ordered by impact. Confirmed facts are separated from my design judgments. P1 means fix before balance sign-off; P2 means improve in the next iteration.

01P1Pacing & finite sinks

The shop runs out of economic purpose.

The catalog is affordable long before the course is finished. Yen keep accumulating, but new chapters mostly release purchases the player can already pay for.

Confirmed

¥48,000 buys all 21 items. In the weekly chapter model, a weekly visitor finishes with ¥86,400 left; a daily visitor has ¥921,600 left. Both own everything on day 42.

Why it disappoints me Cash becomes a second confirmation click after studying, rather than a meaningful choice. The final income boost arrives when almost nothing remains to buy.

What I would change Choose a finite study companion as the primary design. Treat cash as light ceremony, make chapter rewards visibly memorable, and give completion a proper finale. If a lasting tycoon economy is intended, it needs optional, finite stretch goals and another simulation pass before price changes.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Start at ¥0. Make chapter 6 eligible on day 0, then chapters 7–12 every seven days. Collect on each scheduled visit; buy eligible bronze upgrades first, then recipes and decor. Inspect the day-42 wallet and inventory.

E1 · E2 · E4 · Simulation A

02P1Purchase value

Two headline upgrades have no immediate payoff.

The expected chapter order creates two silent income plateaus: the precision knife in chapter 8 and the extended service counter in chapter 10.

Confirmed

Knife: ¥2,400, K3/S2 → K4/S2, income 20 → 20. Counter: ¥5,400, K4/S4 → K4/S6, income 40 → 40. Together they cost ¥7,800, or 26.3% of the six rate upgrades’ total price.

Why it disappoints me Buying extra capacity is a valid strategy, but a chapter’s main prize should feel useful that day. The knife waits for chapter 9; the counter waits for chapter 11 in the expected route.

What I would change Give each a small immediate benefit or present it as a clearly named part of a two-stage milestone. The counter preview also needs an explicit explanation when capacities start equal. A tested arithmetic proposal appears below.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Use the isolated knife fixture, open Shop → Kitchen, buy the knife, and inspect the 20 ¥/min HUD. Repeat with the counter fixture and Shop → Service: the HUD remains 40 ¥/min.

E1 · E2 · E5 · Screens 02–03

03P2First-session pacing

The first renovation takes 30 minutes from zero.

A student who arrives with bronze already earned still starts with an empty wallet. Studying before the restaurant exists does not backfill restaurant income.

Confirmed

The initial restaurant earns 10 ¥/min and the first upgrade costs ¥300: 30 productive minutes, followed by collection and purchase. With no medal, study eligibility is an additional requirement.

Why it disappoints me There is no small renovation to finish during a five- or ten-minute first visit. This is particularly flat for an existing student who has already earned the course reward.

What I would change Prototype a ¥50 first upgrade, giving a five-minute cash target at the unchanged base rate. Keep its bronze requirement. Also explain that income begins when the personal restaurant is created.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Open the fresh fixture: bronze eligibility, ¥0 wallet, no inventory and 10 ¥/min. Compute 300 ÷ 10; no thirty-minute real-time session was needed to establish the wait.

E1 · E2 · E3 · Screen 01

04P2Return rhythm

The cap rewards frequent checking without needing it.

The register stops after eight hours, or twelve after the chapter 7 purchase. Once the cap is reached, waiting longer produces no extra income.

Confirmed

At 20 ¥/min, a 12-hour collection yields ¥14,400. Once daily yields the same ¥14,400 per day; twice daily yields ¥28,800. Once weekly still yields only ¥14,400 per visit. The cap extension adds nothing if all collection gaps are eight hours or shorter.

Why it disappoints me Frequent checking earns more money even though weekly checking already funds the full catalog in the model. That creates avoidable pressure around a resource that soon has little use.

What I would change For the study-companion direction, prototype a 24–48h grace window or kinder full-register messaging, and show the extra stored yen on the cap upgrade. Re-run all cadence models: a longer cap increases surplus further.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Hold the rate fixed at 20 ¥/min and compare 4h, 8h, 12h, 24h and 168h gaps. Earnings equal rate × min(gap, cap). These are opportunity costs against uninterrupted production, not deductions from saved yen.

E2 · E5 · Simulation B

05P2Mastery & recognition

Gold accomplishments compete for two display slots.

Every chapter gives its production feature at bronze. Silver buys a visual recipe; gold buys a decoration. This is intentional, but the display budget is too small for seven chapters of gold.

Confirmed

Seven gold decorations share one wall slot and one floor slot: at most two can be equipped together. No recipe or gold decoration changes income. Gold requires all counted work plus a full best quiz score.

Why it disappoints me I am disappointed that a later gold reward often replaces the visible evidence of an earlier achievement. Keeping power accessible at bronze is sensible; making mastery feel disposable is the weaker part.

What I would change Keep the 60/80/100 thresholds and cosmetic rewards. Add a permanent chapter honor display or collection wall, and reserve a clear place for the final gold trophy. Recognition can accumulate without adding an economic multiplier.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Inspect the current menu: one wall slot and one floor slot. In the completed fixture all seven decorations are owned, but only the chosen wall and floor items are equipped.

E1 · E3 · E5 · Screen 04

06P2Goal quality & theme

The guidance is a checklist, and the learning stays shallow.

“Next goal” selects the first eligible unowned catalog item. It does not compare affordability, bottlenecks or purchase value. Guests cycle through the same three Japanese phrases.

Confirmed

In the knife fixture, the goal points to ¥600 salmon nigiri while the service bottleneck remains unresolved. The phrase list contains only いらっしゃいませ, いただきます and おいしいです, even in the completed restaurant.

Why it disappoints me A cozy collection goal is reasonable, but it should be presented as that. The restaurant currently has little chapter-specific Japanese to discover as the player progresses.

What I would change Offer a choice of “grow the restaurant” and “personalize it,” with a reason for each suggestion. Add optional chapter-linked guest dialogue or recall prompts, using approved course content without silently changing mastery scores or paying for repeated clicks.

Evidence & reproduction ↗

Open the knife fixture before any new purchase: the goal is salmon nigiri. Open the completed fixture, greet a guest and advance phrases; compare the fixed list in the source.

E5 · Screens 02 & 05

There are no claimed progression deadlocks or currency duplication failures in this audit. These priorities describe reward quality and pacing.

The upgrade is worthwhile only when a collection gap exceeds eight hours. It changes storage time, not the minute-by-minute rate. The stopped fraction is foregone production, never a loss from the saved wallet.

At the final rate, 90 ¥/min × 720 minutes = ¥64,800: 135% of the entire catalog. That single comparison is a warning; the cadence simulation is stronger evidence because it accounts for when upgrades and study gates become available.

03 / Purchase value

The two empty steps in the curve

Expected chapter order, with earlier bronze upgrades already owned. “Earn time” starts from zero at the pre-purchase rate; “payback” uses the extra income generated by that purchase.

Chapter Bronze purchase Price ¥/min before → after Income delta Earn time Marginal payback
Ch. 6 Förbättrad beredningsbänk ¥300 10 → 20 +10 30 min 30 min
Ch. 7 Längre produktionstid ¥1,800 20 → 20 0 · +4h storage 90 min —
Ch. 8 Precisionskniv ¥2,400 20 → 20 0 120 min —
Ch. 9 Transportband ¥3,600 20 → 40 +20 180 min 180 min
Ch. 10 Utökad serveringsdisk ¥5,400 40 → 40 0 135 min —
Ch. 11 Assisterande kock ¥7,200 40 → 60 +20 180 min 360 min
Ch. 12 Mästarcertifiering ¥10,800 60 → 90 +30 180 min 360 min

The two +0 capacity purchases are useful later; they are not permanently worthless. A player can defer them until the complementary upgrade is available. “—” means no standalone income payback in that state. Cap payback depends on collection gaps.

What changes for an existing student?

A player with all current medals can receive all purchase grants on first initialization. With no starting yen, a feasible route buys the full catalog in 16h 13m of productive time, collecting at exact affordability. The six rate upgrades are reached in 12h 50m.

This is an accelerated mathematical route, not a prediction that students will actually return at every purchase timestamp. It shows that seven weeks of content gates and the money curve operate on very different clocks.

The script checks all 720 orders of the six rate upgrades and executes the selected route through the real purchase service. Cosmetics and the cap purchase are deferred until the highest rate.

Prototype only · not approved or implemented

A small adjustment to test

Give the knife +1 ¥/order and the service counter +1 ¥/order. Reduce the master license from +5 to +3 ¥/order. Keep capacity changes. The final maximum remains 90 ¥/min.

20→20→22→44→48→72→90

Chapters 6 → 12 · currently 20, 20, 20, 40, 40, 60, 90. This removes the knife/counter income plateaus, but does not fix cash surplus. Separately test a ¥50 first purchase. These are arithmetic-checked hypotheses requiring a fresh cadence simulation and student playtest before adoption.

04 / What I would do next

Make the reward feel earned.

Use the existing study companion brief as the default. Keep current medal rules and permanent grants. These changes are proposals; the audit changes no gameplay.

First · improve the moment

Reward this visit.

Make the first renovation accessible in a short visit, and make every main chapter prize immediately legible.

  • Prototype ¥50 for the prep counter: five productive minutes after restaurant creation, subject to bronze eligibility.
  • Test the knife/counter revenue adjustment above, or clearly pair each with its complementary milestone.
  • Fix the service-counter explanation at equal starting capacities.
Then · improve recognition

Give mastery a home.

Protect the value of gold through expression, not by moving production power behind perfection.

  • Show all seven chapter honors in a persistent display.
  • Offer separate production and personalization goals.
  • Build a visible completion ceremony, then invite a course review rather than another empty collection.
Finally · tune the habit

Respect study rhythms.

Balance around how classmates actually study, including long gaps and students who join with existing medals.

  • Prototype a 24–48h grace cap; re-simulate its extra currency.
  • Add optional chapter-specific guest interactions using approved study material.
  • If a lasting tycoon is desired, define new optional sinks before changing prices.
Proposed acceptance targets · hypotheses, not measured outcomesFirst eligible purchase within 5–10 productive minutes · every main capacity prize has a visible immediate use · all seven gold achievements can remain visible somewhere · weekly visitors never need extra check-ins just to afford the current chapter’s rewards · completion feels complete. Playtest with new, returning and already-qualified students before deciding.

I want the restaurant to remember what a student learned, and make that achievement feel good to come back to.

05 / The current game

Observed, not imagined.

Fresh captures from this audit. Isolated local fixtures used the current catalog and domain service. Images open at full resolution.

Additional captured evidence: the knife’s post-purchase room and full accessibility snapshots for the counter and completed states are saved alongside the report. No production account, payment or deployment was used.

06 / Evidence & limits

What this audit can support

High confidence in current prices, rates, grants and modeled outcomes. Judgments about motivation and satisfaction require real student playtesting.

Scope & limitations

  • Audited the local checkout at commit 1137913, with current source and newly captured screenshots. Production behavior was not tested.
  • Weekly chapter eligibility is an explicit scenario: all three medals become available together. Real students may earn them at different times; the study lock still applies.
  • The in-memory service exercises the production domain rules. Network, callable authorization and live Firestore were outside this balance audit.
  • The local developer login contains starter money. It was used only for the menu capture, never as the initial state in economic calculations. All simulations start at zero.
  • No retention data, student interviews, completion-time distribution or experiment results were available. “Disappointing” is an informed design judgment, not a measured player response.
  • Visual capture and semantic control inspection do not establish full accessibility compliance. A separate keyboard, contrast and screen-reader review would be needed.

One small feedback bug was observed: purchase success announcements calculate the preview against the already-updated state. After buying the knife, the announcement says capacity 5 while the actual state is 4; the counter announcement says 8 while the actual state is 6. This does not change production math. Owner: sushi-view.ts:635.

A documentation caveat: the balance-model document’s claim that a student must complete vocabulary, kanji and grammar to get bronze overstates the current combined-score rule. Its absence of deadlocks is not evidence of satisfying pacing.

Medal weighting: an intentional policy with uneven chapter effects ↗

There is no separate quiz-pass requirement for bronze or silver. Marking all non-quiz items gives silver in chapters 6–9, but only bronze in chapters 10–12 because quizzes form a larger share of the counted items. This is current policy, not a newly discovered exploit. Do not change course scoring merely to tune the restaurant.

Chapter Counted items Bronze ≥ Silver ≥ Gold = All non-quiz items, no quiz
6 90 54 72 90 86.7% · silver
7 92 56 74 92 89.1% · silver
8 68 41 55 68 82.4% · silver
9 67 41 54 67 82.1% · silver
10 66 40 53 66 78.8% · bronze
11 66 40 53 66 78.8% · bronze

Counts were computed from the current course dataset. Vocabulary, kanji, conjugations and individual quiz points are all counted. Progress markings follow the accepted course trust model; the restaurant does not independently verify knowledge. Permanent grants are intentionally not revoked when later practice scores fall.
